reviews.body:
### 🟡 Changes recommended A stale producer can close the new stream’s pipe after Close/Reset, causing io.ErrClosedPipe, and error-path tests do not verify that decompression fails.
2 open issues - [Capture the pipe writer before starting the producer](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/378#discussion_r4712363159) · New - [Assert failed reads produce an invalid gzip stream](https://github.com/Azure/azure-kusto-go/pull/378#discussion_r4712363204) · New
What changed in this PR Fixes gzip-compressed ingestion silently accepting partial input by propagating source read failures through the compressed stream. **Changes:** - Close the output pipe with the underlying error while preserving normal end-of-stream behavior on success. - Skip gzip finalization when source reading fails. - Add a regression test and document the ingestion fix. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `CHANGELOG.md` | Documents the fix for partial ingestion after source read failures. | | `azkustoingest/​internal/​gzip/​gzip.go` | Propagates errors through the pipe and finalizes gzip only after successful reads. | | `azkustoingest/​internal/​gzip/​gzip_test.go` | Adds a failing-reader test that checks source error propagation. |
Review effort: Max

review_comments.body: After `Close` followed by `Reset`, an older producer still blocked in the source's `Read` can close the new stream's pipe here, causing the new stream to fail with `io.ErrClosedPipe`. Capture the pipe writer before launching the producer and use that captured writer for both gzip output and `CloseWithError`.

Checking only the reader error would still pass if `zw.Close()` wrote a valid gzip trailer before the pipe reported that error. Capture the compressed bytes and assert that decompression cannot finish successfully, covering both a read that returns data with an error and an error after a successful read.
